title: The Water of Life (Das Wasser des Lebens)
summary: An old king lay grievously ill, and physicians announced that only the Water of Life from an enchanted castle could restore his failing pulse. His two older sons rode out in turn,...
keywords: the water of life (das wasser des lebens)
full_text:
An old king lay grievously ill, and physicians announced that only the Water of Life from an enchanted castle could restore his failing pulse. His two older sons rode out in turn, puffed up with pride, dreaming only of securing the crown for themselves. Along the trail, each encountered a small dwarf who asked where they were galloping; the haughty princes insulted the dwarf and were consequently led into narrow mountain gorges where their horses could neither advance nor turn back, trapping them in stone canyons.

The youngest prince, riding solely out of pure love for his ailing father, set out next. When he met the little dwarf, he greeted him respectfully and explained his filial quest. The grateful dwarf gave him an iron wand to strike the castle gates three times and two loaves of bread to feed the ravenous lions guarding the inner courtyard. "Enter at the stroke of twelve," warned the dwarf, "and make haste to leave before the clock strikes twelve-and-one, or the gates will shut forever."

The youngest prince pacified the lions, entered the luminous palace, and found an enchanted sleeping princess. She rejoiced at her release, promised to marry him in a year, and told him to draw the Water of Life from the fountain. Escaping just as the clock struck one, the prince rode back with the flask.

Along the road, he used his magical bread and staff to rescue three kingdoms from famine and war, and compassionately secured the release of his imprisoned brothers. But the treacherous older brothers secretly stole the Water of Life while the youngest slept, substituting bitter salt sea-water in his flask. When the father tasted the bitter brine, he grew worse and banished the youngest son in anger, while the brothers claimed the glory.

A year later, the princess laid a road of pure gold before her palace gates, commanding that whoever rode straight down the middle was her true groom. The older brothers, afraid of scratching the gold, rode to the sides and were turned away. The youngest prince, thinking only of his beloved bride, galloped straight over the golden pavement. The joyous princess welcomed him, the old king learned of the treachery, and the humble prince was crowned in honor and everlasting peace.
moral: Kindness to the humble opens doors that pride and arrogance slam shut forever.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Water of Life (Das Wasser des Lebens)"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
